newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra to pay A$3 bln special dividend.
newsitem.headline: Telstra to pay A$3 bln special dividend.

text.p: Australian government owned telecommunications carrier Telstra Corp said on Friday it would pay a special dividend of A$3 billion to the Australian government as part of its partial privatisation process.
Telstra also said it planned to raise the full A$3 billion by June 30 through syndicated loans.
"The new loan raising, which is a syndicated loan, will be for A$3 billion," Telstra Treasurer Cliff Davis told Reuters.
The mandate for the syndicated loan had been given to J.P. Morgan Securities Australia Ltd and Credit Suisse First Boston.
Telstra said that it had a low debt to equity ratio by international comparisons and a larger than necessary reliance on equity.
Davis said the syndicated loan would be made in two tranches, with A$1 billion over a 364 day term and A$2 billion over five years.

Davis said he expected the loan facility would be in place by the end of May and would be drawn down in late June when the A$3 billion payment was made to the government. "I'm planning to have it signed and sealed by the end of May," Davis said.

"The co-arrangers will be going out to the market next week," he said. Davis said this loan and the payment to the government would incease Telstra's debt to equity ratio from its current 30 percent level up to the low 40 percent level.

He said he believed this raising represented the end of the balance sheet restructure and there would not be any more debt raised or special dividends paid before the government's planned privatisation of a third of Telstra before the end of 1997.
"My view is that this is the end of the looking at the capital structure," he said.
The payment to the government would be treated in the Telstra accounts as a payment from retained earnings while debt raised would be treated as a replenishment of working capital.
